qualify verb

be passed as fit, for a post, a profession or a contest

also qualified, be qualified, qualify as, qualify for, qualification, pass as fit

classical

Plin. Ep. 10.30.2 (Trajan): quō prīmum probātī sunt, of recruits passed for service (Lewis & Short)
Caes. BG 7.63.6: ad ūnum Vercingetorīgem probant imperātōrem (Lewis & Short)

probārī (probō, probāre, probāvī, probātum)

passive of a first-conjugation verb

to be approved as fit, pass the test

Probāre is to test and to approve a person as fit (Lewis & Short); the passive is to be passed as fit, as Roman recruits were. Using it of exams for a profession or of a qualifying round is our application. For “qualified” in the sense of fit or suitable, use idōneus with ad (Cic. Lael. 62: ad amīcitiam esse idōneus).

Examples

  • quō prīmum probātī sunt

    on the day they were first passed fit for servicePlin. Ep. 10.30.2, Trajan (Lewis & Short)

See also exam, licence, career, skill.

SourcesLewis & Short: probo · Lewis & Short: idoneus
